data.description:
## Discovered from
bug `conversant-cepivorous-mastiff` (0449-cf75-bb4b-41fd), which widened `claim` to accept a `blocked` source status.

## Problem
The session-provenance triple (`claimed_session`, `claim_harness`, `claim_remote_session`) is keyed to the `open -> in_progress` edge at three sites:
- `_commands/txn.py::claim_core` (write side)
- `_commands/txn.py::transition_core` (`if current_status == "open" and target_status == "in_progress"`)
- `reducer/_processors_status.py::_fold_claimed_session` (`if data.get("current_status") == "open" and data.get("status") == "in_progress"`)

Now that `claim` accepts `blocked`, a blocked-source claim writes `session`/`harness` into the STATUS event but the reducer does NOT fold them into reduced state, so `claimed_session` keeps whatever a previous episode left there (or stays null).

## Why it was NOT fixed under the parent bug
`_fold_claimed_session`'s docstring states the narrow keying is deliberate. Widening it changes **replay semantics for existing historical stores** — a months-old `blocked -> in_progress` transition event would begin clearing `claimed_session` on replay where it previously did not. That is too high a blast radius for a bug fix.

The same staleness already occurs today via the sanctioned `transition blocked in_progress` path, so it is pre-existing, not introduced.

## Scope if taken
Decide whether ANY `* -> in_progress` edge should refresh the provenance triple, and if so migrate all three sites together with an explicit story about historical replay.
data.title: claimed_session provenance is not folded for a blocked-source claim
